title: Main-owned authority lifecycle
summary: How Electron verifies SQLite and consent, recovers Project authority before providers, owns late startup and OpenClaw recovery across Quit, remains windowless, and drains accepted work before close.

chapters.title: Crash-safe startup
chapters.summary: Existing SQLite and consent material is contained, migrated, reconciled, and replayed before structured clients or providers can observe ready state.

chapters.title: Terminal-only safe mode
chapters.summary: Unsafe, future, corrupt, or unverified database state disables structured Agent mutation for the process lifetime while preserving legacy terminal access.

chapters.title: Optional window lifetime
chapters.summary: With keep-running enabled, closing the workbench hides the window while the Electron-main authority continues to own work.

chapters.title: Ordered shutdown
chapters.summary: Quit closes authority, main startup, and local mutation ingress, then dependency-orders Agent, OpenClaw, desktop, and SQLite cleanup behind their accepted work.

states.label: Persisted daemon material
states.detail: SQLite, WAL sidecars, the atomic external Workspace consent journal, and named legacy sources remain under contained user-data recovery boundaries.

evidence.claim: DaemonStoreRecovery owns the contained filesystem boundary for exact SQLite material and explicitly named legacy inputs.
The bounded v2 access file stores committed grants and pending approval or revocation intents together in the same atomic JSON material.

states.label: Verifying and recovering store
states.detail: Containment, integrity, backup, schema migration, uncertain-command recovery, and consent-journal validation must finish before the authority can become ready.

evidence.claim: Initialization validates containment and existing database material, rejects future schemas, and requires a verified migration or legacy backup before mutation.
The store opens with strict SQLite options, enables WAL and full synchronization, migrates, recovers uncertain commands, then marks itself ready.
Consent validation bounds entries and intents, rejects inconsistent revocations, and migrates a valid v1 grant file to an empty v2 pending list.

states.label: Structured authority ready
states.detail: Pending Workspace consent has recovered and Project sync has settled before the router, shared ownership gate, Project FIFO, MCP, Agents, and automation become live.

evidence.claim: Main recovers pending consent and synchronizes Projects before the ordered MCP, Agent, and automation startup publishes ready availability and binds the exact shutdown barrier.
Agent startup restores provider subscriptions, expires approvals, repairs claims, rehydrates Sessions, reconciles unsettled work, and rearms durable timeouts.
The Project-operation FIFO rejects new work after shutdown begins, preserves its exact accepted prefix, and serializes both successful and failed predecessors.

states.label: Terminal-only safe mode
states.detail: The failure and database disposition are latched; structured Agent reads and writes stop while legacy terminal operation remains available.

evidence.claim: Any structured-store initialization error becomes a stable legacy-only safe-mode availability record with its database disposition.
Desktop clients can still read availability, while structured snapshot and command paths return unavailable or reject with the terminal-only safe-mode reason.
Main reports structured authority failure as a terminal-preserving safe mode rather than failing the entire desktop runtime.

states.label: Window hidden, daemon running
states.detail: With explicit keep-running preference, closing the main window hides it without ending provider or terminal processes.

evidence.claim: The main-window close policy hides only when keepRunning is enabled; opening restores, shows, and focuses the same authority client window.

states.label: Ingress closed and draining
states.detail: Quit closes authority, main-owned startup, and local mutation ingress synchronously; accepted Project, Agent, automation, provider, and recovery work drains once.

evidence.claim: The idempotent authority barrier aborts late startup, closes command, provider, and Agent ingress, then drains automation, startup, Agent persistence, and both early and late MCP instances.
The main-owned startup barrier rejects late publication through abort checkpoints, drains admitted startup, and releases tracked subscriptions afterward.
Local mutation ingress closes synchronously, aborts cancellable work, denies later admission, and resolves one stable drain after every accepted callback settles.

states.label: Authority and SQLite closed
states.detail: Normal SQLite close waits exact writer drains; the process exit gate also bounds dependency-ordered cleanup while OpenClaw recovery is owned through disposal.

evidence.claim: The close helper awaits the exact authority stop plus every concurrent drain before preparing and closing the store.
Main closes ingress first and dependency-orders service disposal; DaemonStore waits exact authority and writer drains, while OpenClaw cleanup follows the startup barrier.
OpenClaw disposal closes publication synchronously, awaits initialization and pending bootstrap recovery, then flushes both atomic control files.
DaemonStore serializes initialization, latches a structured failure, and never exposes a partially initialized database.
Successful database, consent recovery, and Project synchronization gate the ordered start and ready publication of every structured Agent runtime.
Any rejected structured-authority preflight or startup becomes one process-lifetime safe-mode availability record and is logged while legacy terminals remain enabled.
Closing the main window hides it only when keepRunning is true; otherwise the same event requests application Quit.
Reopening creates a missing window or restores, shows, and focuses the existing renderer client.
The first Quit task synchronously closes Project, main-startup, local-Agent, and Project-Map ingress before their dependent drains run.
Explicit Quit requests application shutdown, whose process owner stops all registered daemon resources exactly once.
When no writable authority exists, safe-mode shutdown selects process-loss cleanup so it releases providers without attempting structured database writes.
SQLite closure cannot run until the authoritative stop promise and all concurrent writer drains resolve.
Shutdown validates and runs named task dependencies, falls back to declared order for an invalid graph, and opens the exit gate after completion or its bounded timeout.
Main closes ingress first, drains main startup and local mutations, and orders OpenClaw and desktop cleanup while DaemonStore awaits the exact authority and concurrent writer barrier.
